title: Slice pullback of an inner anodyne map is categorically equivalent
statement: Use simplicial sets, quasicategories, categorical equivalences and inner anodyne maps in the conventions of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure] and [lem-coef-inner-anodyne-pushout-product]. Let $C$ be a quasicategory, let $c$ be a vertex of $C$, let $i:L\hookrightarrow K$ be an inner anodyne inclusion of small simplicial sets, and let $\delta:K\to C$ be a simplicial map. Form $C_{/c}$ from simplices $\Delta^n\star\Delta^0\to C$ ending at $c$, projected by the entire first face, and put $K_{/c}=K\times_C C_{/c}$ and $L_{/c}=L\times_C C_{/c}$. Then the induced inclusion $i_c:L_{/c}\hookrightarrow K_{/c}$ is a categorical equivalence in the Joyal sense. No quasicategory hypothesis is imposed on $L$, $K$, $K_{/c}$ or $L_{/c}$.

source.place: Proposition 7.3.1.14 (02YL), proof first paragraph, using Corollary 5.6.7.6 for pullback along the slice right fibration

proof.text: Let $p$ be a fibration of the Joyal model structure of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. That node makes every inner horn inclusion $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, $0<i<n$, a trivial cofibration, and fibrations have the right lifting property against trivial cofibrations; hence $p$ has the right lifting property against every inner horn, i.e. $p$ is an inner fibration in the sense of [lem-coef-inner-anodyne-pushout-product]. Since $i$ is inner anodyne, it has the left lifting property against every inner fibration of [lem-coef-inner-anodyne-pushout-product], in particular against every Joyal fibration. By the weak factorization system (trivial cofibrations, fibrations) of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure], the maps with the left lifting property against all fibrations are exactly the trivial cofibrations, so $i$ is a trivial cofibration, in particular a Joyal weak equivalence; by the same node these weak equivalences are exactly the categorical equivalences. Thus $i:L\to K$ is a categorical equivalence.

source.place: Proposition 7.3.1.14 (02YL), first paragraph: the inner anodyne inclusion is a categorical equivalence (lifting-class argument in the Joyal model structure)

proof.text: The slice construction with $K=\Delta^0$ and $p=c$ gives a quasicategory $C_{/c}$ and a right fibration $q:C_{/c}\to C$ by [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration]. Apply the right-fibration pullback theorem [lem-coef-right-fibration-categorical-base-change] to the categorical equivalence $i:L\to K$ over $C$ and this $q$. It gives that $L\times_C C_{/c}\to K\times_C C_{/c}$ is a categorical equivalence. The theorem is stated for arbitrary simplicial sets $L$ and $K$ and does not assume that either pullback is a quasicategory, exactly matching the present hypotheses.

source.place: Proposition 7.3.1.14 (02YL), first paragraph, using Corollary 5.6.7.6 (dual right-fibration pullback form)

proof.text: By the degreewise pullback convention, the map in Step 2 is exactly the induced inclusion $i_c:L_{/c}\hookrightarrow K_{/c}$ defined in the statement. The argument used only that $C$ is a quasicategory, that $c$ is a vertex, and that $i$ is inner anodyne; no quasicategory condition on $L$, $K$, or either pullback was introduced.
